# The least positive Mahler measure in the group generated by two Chebyshev units

Recorded at 2026-11-24T17:35 UTC.

<a id="minimum"></a>
## The minimum over all exponent pairs

Let \(q\) be a positive integer, \(p=q+1\), \(M=pq\), and \(L=p+q\).
Take any even \(n\ge4\) satisfying \(4^{n-1}\le2M\), and put \(d=n-3\).
Using the Chebyshev polynomials \(U_j\) of the second kind, form the [endpoint modification](../ledger/Yin_L_G0462_v324.md#repair)
\[
 B_j(x)=U_j((x+2)/2),\quad C_d=B_d+B_{d-1},\qquad
 H(x)=x^{n-1}(x+4)+2(Mx-1)C_d(x).
\]
Let \(w\) be the positive root of \(H\) below \(1/M\), and define \(T>1\) and \(Y\) by
\[
 T+T^{-1}=2+w,\qquad Y=\frac{pT-q}{p-qT}.
\]
Write \(m(\alpha)\) for the total logarithmic Mahler measure of the primitive minimal polynomial of \(\alpha\).
For all sufficiently large \(q\), uniformly over the allowed degrees,
\[
 \min_{(a,b)\in\mathbb Z^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}}m(T^aY^b)
 =m(T)=\log(2M)+M^{-1/2}+O(n^2/M).
\]
Exactly the exponent pairs \((1,0)\) and \((-1,0)\) attain this minimum.
Allowing an arbitrary root of unity as an additional factor for each exponent pair gives the same minimum.
Thus the least positive measure in these groups diverges even though the distinguished value of \(T\) tends to one.

<a id="conjugates"></a>
## Conjugates and the measure of \(T\)

The recurrence \(B_{j+1}=(x+2)B_j-B_{j-1}\), with \(B_0=1\) and \(B_1=x+2\), gives monic integral polynomials and \(C_d(0)=2d+1\).
The polynomial \(H\) is monic, its nonleading coefficients are even, and its constant coefficient is \(-2(2d+1)\), so it is Eisenstein at two.
The signs \(H(0)<0<H(1/M)\) give the required positive root \(w\).

For \(x=2\cos\theta-2\), one has \(C_d(x)=\sin((2d+1)\theta/2)/\sin(\theta/2)\).
At \(\theta_j=(2j+1)\pi/(2d+1)\), \(0\le j\le d\), its values alternate in sign and have absolute value at least one.
Here \(-4\le x<0\) and
\[
 |x^{n-1}(x+4)|\le4^{n-1}|x|\le2M|x|<2|Mx-1|.
\]
The \(d\) intervening intervals therefore give \(d\) distinct roots of \(H\) in \((-4,0)\).
The coefficients of \(x^{n-1}\) and \(x^{n-2}\) are \(4\) and \(2M\), so the sums of the roots and their squares are \(-4\) and \(16-4M<0\), respectively.
The remaining two roots must be nonreal conjugates.
In particular \(w\) is the only positive root.

Write the nonreal traces as \(\xi=A+iB,\bar\xi\), and write \(t_i\) for the \(n-2\) real roots, including \(w\).
The same two sums give
\[
 2A=-4-\sum_i t_i,\qquad B^2=2M-8+A^2+\tfrac12\sum_i t_i^2 .
\]
Since \(|t_i|\le4\), one has \(A=O(n)\) and \(|2+\xi|^2=2M+O(n^2)\).
The discriminant \(w(w+4)\) of \(X^2-(2+w)X+1\) is negative at a real embedding of \(\mathbb Q(w)\) corresponding to a root in \((-4,0)\).
It cannot be a square in \(\mathbb Q(w)\), so \(X^nH(X+X^{-1}-2)\) is monic of degree \(2n=[\mathbb Q(T):\mathbb Q]\) and is the minimal polynomial of \(T\).
Its constant coefficient is one, so \(T\) is a unit.
Each negative real trace gives two roots on the unit circle.
Over \(\xi\), let \(\zeta+\zeta^{-1}=2+\xi\) with \(r=|\zeta|>1\).
The roots over \(\bar\xi\) are the complex conjugates of those over \(\xi\).
Since \(\big||2+\xi|^2-r^2\big|\le 2+r^{-2}\), all exterior roots together give
\[
 r^2=2M+O(n^2),\qquad m(T)=\log T+2\log r.
\]

For \(x\ge0\), writing \(2+x=2\cosh s\) gives \(B_j(x)\ge j+1\) from the hyperbolic sine formula, with equality at \(s=0\).
Thus \(C_d(w)\ge2d+1\), and \(H(w)=0\) gives
\[
 0<1-Mw=\frac{w^{n-1}(w+4)}{2C_d(w)}=O(M^{1-n}).
\]
It follows that \(w=M^{-1}+O(M^{-n})\).
Using \(\log T=2\operatorname{arsinh}(\sqrt w/2)\) and \(n=O(\log M)\), we obtain, with absolute implied constants,
\[
 \log T=M^{-1/2}+O(M^{-3/2}),\qquad
 \log r=\tfrac12\log(2M)+O(n^2/M).
\]
These identities give the asserted expansion for \(m(T)\).

<a id="products"></a>
## Lower bounds at two embeddings

The inequalities \(0<w<1/M=p/q+q/p-2\) give \(1<T<p/q\), so \(Y>1\).
Writing \(\delta=1-Mw\), direct substitution gives
\[
 N_{\mathbb Q(w)/\mathbb Q}(\delta)=M^nH(1/M)=4M+1=L^2,\qquad
 Y+Y^{-1}-2=\frac{L^2w}{\delta}.
\]
The quotient \(L^2/\delta\) is an algebraic integer since it is the product of the other conjugates of \(\delta\).
Both \(Y\) and \(Y^{-1}\) thus satisfy a monic quadratic with algebraic integer coefficients, so \(Y\) is a unit.
Since \(L^2w\) is bounded below by a positive absolute constant for large \(M\), the upper bound for \(\delta\) gives
\[
 y_0:=\log Y\ge(n-1)\log M-O(1).
\]
At the embedding \(T\mapsto\zeta\), put \(Y_\zeta=(p\zeta-q)/(p-q\zeta)\).
The identity
\[
 Y_\zeta+\frac pq=\frac{L}{q(p-q\zeta)}
\]
and \(r^2=2M+O(n^2)\) give \(|Y_\zeta+p/q|=O(M^{-1})\) and \(y_1:=\log|Y_\zeta|=O(M^{-1/2})\).

Put \(t_0=\log T\) and \(t_1=\log r\).
The nontrivial automorphism of \(\mathbb Q(T)/\mathbb Q(w)\) takes \(T\) to \(T^{-1}\) and \(Y\) to \(Y^{-1}\).
At both selected embeddings it supplies the opposite logarithm as another conjugate value for \(Z=T^aY^b\).
Hence \(m(Z)\ge |a t_j+b y_j|\) for \(j=0,1\), including when \(Z\) belongs to a proper subfield.
Any root-of-unity factor of \(Z\) preserves these two lower bounds, since each embedding extends to the compositum with the cyclotomic field and every image of the root of unity has modulus one.

Suppose \(b\ne0\).
If \(|a|\ge3|b|\), then \(m(Z)\ge3|b|(t_1-|y_1|)>m(T)\) for all sufficiently large \(q\).
If \(|a|<3|b|\), then \(m(Z)\ge |b|(y_0-3t_0)>m(T)\), since \(n\ge4\).
Both comparisons are uniform since \(n=O(\log M)\).

For large \(q\), \(1<T<r\), and the list of conjugates shows that \(T\) is the unique conjugate with modulus \(T\).
For any nonzero integer \(a\), every embedding of \(\mathbb Q(T)\) fixing \(T^a\) must therefore fix \(T\).
This gives \(\mathbb Q(T^a)=\mathbb Q(T)\) and \(m(T^a)=|a|m(T)\), using inversion for \(a<0\).
For a root of unity \(\omega\) of order \(k\), the total measure satisfies \(m(\alpha^k)\le k\,m(\alpha)\) because powering multiplies absolute logarithmic height by \(k\) and can only lower the degree.
Taking \(\alpha=\omega T^a\) gives \(m(\omega T^a)\ge m(T^{ak})/k=|a|m(T)\).
The two cases establish the minimum, and \(T\) itself attains it with or without the option of a torsion factor.
